title: It’s been a week since I saw Come From Away in Gander and it’s taken ...
transcript: I've always loved Come From Away, but nothing could have prepared me for the feeling of watching this musical in Gander, Newfoundland, surrounded by the community that made it possible. If you've never seen Come From Away, it's a musical inspired by the true story of the nearly 7,000 airline passengers whose plans were diverted to the small town of Gander, Newfoundland, on September 11th, 2,001. 9 11 is a tragedy beyond comprehension. But what happened in the days that followed in Gander is a reminder that even in humanity's darkest moments, extraordinary goodness is still possible. And being in Gander, hearing the stories firsthand, seeing the places with my own eyes and feeling the warmth of the community made this musical resonate in entirely new ways. And this is a Newfoundland production of Come From Away. Director Julie and Kylie talked about it before the show, saying she wanted it to feel like a warm embrace. They even asked Newfoundlanders to send in granny squares to decorate the set. They wanted 100. We got 23 squares. So there's all kinds of little touches like that. This, the gander clock, is here that you might see from the airport. The theater can be a little bit chilly, and the actors got together and said, well, we. We can crochet. We're gonna sew together a bunch of the squares and make little blankets. Aren't they sweet? And I'm hoping if anybody needs a blanket over their shoulders, the ushers here have some In their hands. There they are. And, you know, just put up your hand and a little bit of the warm embrace right over your shoulders. And that's exactly how this production feels. More homegrown, more intimate, more Newfoundland. And instead of being a musical where we learn this story, it's a musical where they're telling their own story. Company is about 50% Newfoundlanders, the majority Canadian. There are two members of the original Broadway cast. There are two members of the original Broadway orchestra. My favorite part though, was just watching this show in a theater full of Newfoundlanders. Cause they weren't just laughing at jokes, they were recognizing their neighbours, their traditions, their sense of humour and the immense kindness that has defined Newfoundland for generations. It was the best kind of theatre and one I will remember for the rest of my life.
